lessons.title: Comprehension: A Saturday at the market
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level II (Class 4) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Read a short passage and answer questions.
Answer in full sentences using words from the text.
reviewNotes: Original passage written for CastBridge; no real people. Check reading level against the textbook.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.md: Every Saturday, Ngum goes to the market in Bafoussam with his mother. The market opens at six o'clock and it is full of people. Women sell tomatoes, yams and fresh fish. Men sell shoes and clothes. A boy carries a heavy bag of maize on his head. Ngum's mother buys a bunch of plantains and some onions. Then Ngum buys a cold drink. 'What a busy morning!' says his mother with a smile.

blocks.title: How to answer
blocks.md: Read the passage **twice**. Read each question carefully and look for the key words in the passage. Answer with a **full sentence**. For *who, what, where, when* find the fact in the text. For *why* look for a reason: *because*. If a word is new, use the other words in the sentence to guess its meaning.

items.text: 3. Find the answer in the passage

blocks.caption: Four steps for comprehension.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: read the passage twice, read the question, find the answer, write a full sentence.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Writing an answer from memory instead of checking the passage.
- Copying a whole paragraph: use only the part that answers the question.
- Answering with one word when a full sentence is asked.
- Mixing up the people: Ngum is the boy, the mother buys the plantains.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Question: Where does Ngum go on Saturday?
steps: Look for 'Saturday' and 'goes' in the passage: Ngum goes to the market in Bafoussam.
blocks.answer: Ngum goes to the market in Bafoussam on Saturday.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Question: Why does Ngum's mother say 'What a busy morning!'?
steps: Look at the sentence before: the market is full of people and many things happen.
blocks.answer: She says it because the market is full of busy people.

lessons.title: Comprehension: Ada and the river
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level II (Class 4) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Understand the main idea and order of events of a story.
Say what a character is like from what she does.
Guess the meaning of new words from the text.
reviewNotes: Original story; the moral (kindness) is simple on purpose.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.md: Ada lived near a small river. One dry season, the river became very low and the village ran short of water. The people walked a long way to find water. Ada did not complain. She woke up early and carried a small bucket. On the way she shared some water with an old man who was tired. When the rains came, the river was full again. The old man thanked Ada and told everyone how kind she was.

items.text: Ada shares water with an old man
The rains come; everyone knows her kindness

blocks.caption: The three parts of the story.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: beginning, the village has little water; middle, Ada shares water with an old man; end, the rains come and everyone knows her kindness.

blocks.title: Types of questions
blocks.md: **Fact questions** (who, what, where, when): the answer is in the text. **Why / how questions**: look for the reason. **Meaning of a word**: read the sentence around it. **Character questions**: what the person does shows what she is like. **Title questions**: choose a short title that tells the main idea.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Answering with your own idea when the passage gives the answer.
- Choosing a word meaning that does not fit the sentence.
- Mixing the order of events: use first, then, at last.
- Writing opinions as if they were facts.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Why did the village run short of water?
steps: Look at the second sentence: the river became very low in the dry season.
blocks.answer: Because the river became very low in the dry season.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: What kind of girl is Ada? Give one proof.
steps: Ada shares her water with a tired old man.
This shows that she is kind (and she did not complain, so she is also patient).
blocks.answer: Ada is kind: she shared her water with the old man.
